meta.title: Courts and the government
meta.question: Should the courts be able to stop the government?
meta.measure: Average position on judicial independence, from 0 (independent courts) to 10 (government influence over the courts)
meta.anchor: Pooled from questions on whether the courts and the Constitutional Tribunal should be able to stop the government, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: Should the Sejm have the right to reject rulings of the Constitutional Tribunal, or should the Tribunal's rulings be final?
items.notes: CBOS, January 1995, 1 survey (before the 1997 constitution the Sejm could overturn Tribunal rulings by a two-thirds vote).

items.wording: Is the Constitutional Tribunal needed for the state to function well, or does it hinder efficient government?
items.notes: CBOS, January 1995 and April 2016 (APiW 311), 2 surveys: the only repeated CBOS question on the courts and the government, before and after the Tribunal crisis.

items.wording: If the Constitutional Tribunal made decisions most people disagreed with, it would be better to do away with it (agree-disagree)
People should obey Constitutional Tribunal decisions even when they disagree (agree-disagree)
It is everyone's duty to back the decisions of the courts, even when they disagree with them (agree-disagree)
items.notes: European Social Survey round 5 (2010), 1 survey; from the justice module, about criminal courts. The counterpart of PGSW_TRIBUNAL_OBEY; leave out if the attitude is to stay strictly about courts versus government.

items.wording: In an ideal democracy, are the government's actions controlled by the Constitutional Tribunal?
How important for democracy in general is it that the courts are able to stop the government acting beyond its authority? (0-10)
items.notes: European Social Survey round 6 (2012), 1 survey; the item of PGSW_CONSTCOURT_IMP.

items.wording: How important for democracy is it that constitutional courts can stop the government acting beyond its powers? (0-10)
Prime Minister Beata Szydło did not publish the Constitutional Tribunal's ruling that PiS's amendment of the Tribunal act was unconstitutional: was she right or wrong?
items.notes: CBOS, April 2016, 1 survey. A concrete case of a government ignoring a court ruling; strongly partisan.

items.wording: Is it a good idea for parliament, rather than assemblies of judges as until now, to elect the judges of the National Council of the Judiciary?
Independent judges should be able to overrule the decisions of a democratically elected government if they violate the constitution (agree-disagree)
items.notes: European Election Study 2019 (online), 1 survey; the item of EES_JUDGES (2024).

items.wording: How important for calling a state democratic: control of the government's actions by independent courts, including the Constitutional Tribunal (very important ... not a feature of democracy at all)
items.notes: CBOS democracy survey, about 2021 (SINGLE), 1 survey. Its twin on whether this holds in Poland (q114) is a perception and is left out.

items.wording: Is it a good idea for parliament, rather than assemblies of judges as until now, to elect the judges of the National Council of the Judiciary?
items.notes: CBOS's mixed-mode surveys (CAPI, CATI or CAWI, the respondent's choice) from APiW 359 (May-June 2020), so a question of its own.

items.wording: How important for democracy is it that constitutional courts can stop the government when it exceeds its powers? (0-10)
items.notes: NCN Opus online panel, waves 1 and 3, 2 surveys; the ESS/PGSW wording. Identical copies (A2_B_1, essgen2_1).

items.wording: The government should be able to ignore court rulings that are seen as politically biased (agree-disagree)
items.notes: NCN Opus online panel, waves 1-3 (2023-24), 3 surveys of the same panel; wave 3 asked about half. Identical copies (A1_M_*, JUDCNSTR2_*): the first is used. The conjoint attribute variables (Item17_*, Item27_*) carry this text only in their value labels and are not matched.

items.wording: Courts should be able to stop government actions that exceed its powers (agree-disagree)
Judges should be able to overrule government decisions (agree-disagree)
The government should be able to ignore court rulings that are seen as politically biased (agree-disagree)
items.notes: FNW SWPS online survey, May 2025, 1 survey (coded the other way round from NCN).

items.wording: How much influence should politicians have over the courts? 1 = courts fully independent of politics, politicians have no say over who becomes a judge ... 7 = democratically elected politicians should have influence over the courts and who becomes a judge
items.notes: FNW SWPS online survey, May 2026, 1 survey.
